answer: Personalized prompts: each epoch the protocol derives a fresh seed from every identity's address and uses it to pick that identity's required words, say fable, ferrous and canyon. Peers attest an answer only if it is coherent and uses its own words, and a similarity check flags near-duplicates across identities. So one good text cannot be pasted into a hundred clones; each extra identity needs a separately written answer every epoch, a recurring labor cost. Limit: cheap text generators shrink that cost, so graders must still judge substance, not word presence.
